summary.text: This paper reports a case of a 43-year-old woman with undiagnosed mitral valve prolapse (MVP) who experienced ventricular ectopic beats during total abdominal hysterectomy under regional anaesthesia. The patient remained haemodynamically stable, and the surgical procedure was completed uneventfully. Postoperative transthoracic echocardiography revealed previously undiagnosed mitral valve prolapse.

The authors highlight the importance of vigilant intraoperative monitoring and consideration of underlying structural cardiac abnormalities when unexplained ventricular arrhythmias occur during regional anaesthesia.
The paper emphasizes the need for early recognition and management of potential complications to ensure safe perioperative management.
The authors discuss the prevalence and clinical outcome of mitral-valve prolapse, as well as the importance of echocardiography in risk stratification.
The paper reviews the literature on mitral valve prolapse, including its diagnosis, management, and perioperative implications.
